xtal.desc: Crystal 12 MHz ±30 ppm, CL 10 pF, ESR 50 ohm max, 3.2x2.5 mm 4-SMD
xtal.notes: Checked 2026-11-10. DigiKey: Active, 23,471 in stock (constrained supply, no backorders). Mouser: 8,620 in stock. LCSC: 1,455 in stock. Datasheet rev B: load capacitance 10 pF, ESR (R1) 50 ohm max, C0 3.0 pF max, drive level 10 uW typ / 200 uW max, tolerance and stability ±30 ppm, -40 to +85 C. Pad mapping (datasheet top view): pads 1 and 3 are the crystal, pads 2 and 4 are GND (lid). Pad 1 bottom-left, 2 bottom-right, 3 top-right, 4 top-left, which is the same numbering and position as KiCad Crystal:Crystal_SMD_3225-4Pin_3.2x2.5mm (pad 1 at -1.1,+0.85; 2 at +1.1,+0.85; 3 at +1.1,-0.85; 4 at -1.1,-0.85). The footprint matches with no remapping. The crystal is symmetric, so 180 degree rotation is harmless. Datasheet says the body chamfer can sit on pin 1, 3 or 4, so it is not a reliable orientation mark.

ind.desc: Inductor 3.3 uH ±20%, Isat 2.4 A, Irms 2.1 A, DCR 140 mohm max, shielded molded, polarity dot, 2016 (0806)
ind.notes: Checked 2026-11-10. DigiKey: Active, 3,426 in stock. Mouser: 18,018 in stock. LCSC: only 10 in stock (1,328 more via 'other suppliers', 3-5 days), so buy from Mouser or DigiKey. Polarity: confirmed. Datasheet rev A has a 'Marking (White Ink polarity dot)' section; the dot is on the top face in the corner next to one terminal, and the datasheet labels that terminal '+' (current drawn entering there). Parts are taped with the dot aligned the same way. The datasheet does not number the terminals. KiCad footprint Inductor_SMD:L_Abracon_AOTA-B201610S has two identical pads (1 at x=-0.75, 2 at x=+0.75, 0.8x1.6 mm) and NO polarity mark on silk or fab, so the board needs its own dot mark and the assembler needs an explicit note. Datasheet land pattern is 1.0x1.6 mm pads with a 1.0 mm gap; the KiCad pads are 0.8 mm wide with a 0.7 mm gap. Raspberry Pi hardware design guide, Figure 4 (PCB layout of the regulator, page 6): L1 pad 2 is on net VREG_LX and pad 1 is on +1V1, and the polarity dot is drawn at the pad 1 end. So Raspberry Pi puts the dot end on the 1V1 output (C7 side) and the non-dot end on VREG_LX. The guide's text does not state this in words; it comes from the figure only, so check against Raspberry Pi's minimal-design KiCad files before release. No drop-in replacement: this is the only polarity-marked part Raspberry Pi names.

led_g.desc: LED green 525 nm InGaN, 430 mcd typ and Vf 3.2 V typ at 20 mA, 140 deg, water clear, 0603
led_g.notes: Checked 2026-11-10. DigiKey: Active, 198,792 in stock. Mouser: 537,909 in stock. LCSC: not carried (search returns 0 results). Well stocked, no replacement needed. Datasheet: Vf 3.2 V typ / 3.5 V max at 20 mA, 220 mcd min / 430 mcd typ at 20 mA, 30 mA max continuous, MSL 3, pad 1 cathode (polarity mark), pad 2 anode. Low-current figures are ESTIMATES scaled from the 20 mA values, because the datasheet curves could not be read as numbers: about 2.6 to 2.8 V and roughly 10 to 20 mcd at 0.5 to 1 mA. That is clearly visible indoors. On a 3.3 V rail the headroom is only about 0.5 V, so use about 1 k (roughly 0.5 mA); from 5 V use 2.2 k to 4.7 k.

led_a.desc: LED amber 605 nm AlInGaP, 130 mcd typ and Vf 2.0 V typ at 20 mA, 140 deg, water clear, 0603
led_a.notes: Checked 2026-11-10. DigiKey: Active, 35,751 in stock. Mouser (mouser.co.uk page): 97,451 in stock. LCSC: not carried (search returns 0 results). Well stocked, no replacement needed. Datasheet: Vf 2.0 V typ / 2.4 V max at 20 mA, 70 mcd min / 130 mcd typ at 20 mA, 30 mA max continuous, MSL 3, pad 1 cathode (polarity mark), pad 2 anode. Low-current figures are ESTIMATES scaled from the 20 mA values, because the datasheet curves could not be read as numbers: about 1.8 V and roughly 3 to 6 mcd at 0.5 to 1 mA. That is 3 to 4 times dimmer than the green LED at the same current. To look balanced next to the green one, run amber near 1 mA or more (1.5 k from 3.3 V gives about 1 mA; 2.2 k to 3.3 k from 5 V) and green near 0.5 mA.
